title: Triage Copilot: LLM rolling summaries of production logs for on-call
context: Internal tooling for a mid-size B2B SaaS. The platform team is 2 engineers; per the team charter both are in the weekly on-call rotation and on-call/interrupt work averages 50% of their time. Goal: cut incident MTTR (currently median 47 min). Approved tooling budget for this initiative: $1,500/month run cost. This plan is about to be dispatched for a 6-week build.
artifact:
# Triage Copilot — build plan

Owner: Platform | 6 weeks | Start: Monday after approval

## 1. Goal
Give the on-call engineer a plain-language "what is going wrong right now" summary within seconds of a page, instead of spending the first 15-20 minutes grepping logs across 30 services.
Target: median MTTR 47 min -> 30 min within one quarter of launch.

## 2. How it works
- log-tap (new): subscribes to the existing Vector pipeline after the redaction stage and forwards every application log line to the summarizer queue.
- summarizer (new): every 5 minutes, sends the last 5 minutes of logs per service to the LLM with a fixed prompt and stores a structured summary (top errors, new error signatures, affected endpoints, suspected deploy).
- On page: the PagerDuty incident gets an auto-comment with the latest summaries for the paging service and its direct dependencies (from the service catalog).
- Summaries are advisory only. Alert rules, paging, and escalation policies are unchanged.

## 3. Volumes
- Application logs: 38M lines/day average across 30 services (peak day 61M).
- Average line length: ~60 tokens after redaction.
- Model: Corvid-mini, $0.50 per 1M input tokens, $2.00 per 1M output tokens.
- Output: ~400 tokens per summary, 30 services x 288 windows/day = 8,640 summaries/day.

## 4. Cost
- Input: 38M lines x 60 tokens = 2.28B tokens -> ~$1,140
- Output: 8,640 x 400 = 3.5M tokens -> ~$7
- Queue + storage: existing Redis and Postgres, negligible.
- Estimated total: ~$1,150/month, within the $1,500 budget.

## 5. Privacy
- log-tap reads only after the Vector redaction stage, which already masks emails, tokens, card numbers and IPs for our log retention policy (audited in Q1).
- Corvid account has zero-retention enabled; data processing addendum signed by Legal (ref DPA-0417).

## 6. Staffing and estimate
| Work item                               | Eng-weeks |
|-----------------------------------------|-----------|
| log-tap + queue                         | 2         |
| summarizer + prompt + storage           | 4         |
| PagerDuty integration + service catalog | 2         |
| Eval set from last 40 incidents         | 2         |
| Hardening, dashboards, runbook          | 2         |
| Total                                   | 12        |

Staffing: both platform engineers full-time for 6 weeks (2 x 6 = 12 eng-weeks).

## 7. Evaluation
Before launch, replay the last 40 incidents: for each, generate the summary that would have been attached at page time and have the incident commander grade it (useful / partially / misleading). Launch gate: >= 70% useful, <= 5% misleading.

defects.description: Cross-reference §3 vs §4: 2.28B input tokens is a per-DAY volume (38M lines/day), so input cost is ~$1,140/day, roughly $34k/month (more on 61M-line peaks), not ~$1,150/month. The run cost exceeds the $1,500/month budget by ~20x and the design needs sampling/filtering before it is viable.

Cross-reference context vs §6: the estimate assumes both engineers full-time for 6 weeks, but the team charter puts both in the on-call rotation with ~50% interrupt load. Real capacity is ~6 eng-weeks, so the 12 eng-week plan will take ~12 weeks or silently drop the eval/hardening work.
defects.evidence: Staffing: both platform engineers full-time for 6 weeks (2 x 6 = 12 eng-weeks).

decoys: Sending production logs (PII, secrets) to a third-party LLM: handled in §5 — logs are tapped after the audited redaction stage and the provider has zero retention plus a signed DPA.
Hallucinated summaries misleading on-call: handled in §2 and §7 — summaries are advisory, paging unchanged, and a 40-incident replay eval with a misleading-rate launch gate.
